questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best types of exercise for heart health
How to choose a comfortable office chair
Why sitting too much harms our health
Why people in Britain watch too much television
questions.why: They find out how much sitting is too much and how it affects our health.

questions.q: What does Phil say about his own habits?
options: He exercises every day
He never does any kind of exercise at all
He works standing up
He cycles at weekends but sits a lot
questions.why: He rides his bike at the weekend but admits he spends a lot of time sitting down.

questions.q: Why are we sitting so much, according to Professor Charlotte Edwardson?
options: People are lazier than in the past
Technology has removed much of the movement from daily life
Doctors tell us to rest more
Office chairs today are much more comfortable than they used to be
questions.why: She says movement has been engineered out of our everyday lives by advances in technology.

questions.q: What happens when we sit down, according to Professor Edwardson?
options: Big muscles aren't used, so blood flow falls
Our heart beats faster
Our leg muscles work harder and grow stronger
We burn more energy
questions.why: We don't use the large muscles in our legs and bum, so circulation reduces.

questions.q: How much more energy does the body use when standing than when sitting?
options: About 92% more
About 60% more
About 5% more
About 20% more
questions.why: Georgie says the body uses 20% more energy when standing; walking uses 92% more.

questions.q: Why does Professor Edwardson mention meetings and doctors' surgeries?
options: To show how much of daily life is organised around sitting
To say these places should have more chairs
To explain where people catch illnesses
To suggest that doctors and business people should sit down less
questions.why: People always say “Come and take a seat” – everything's geared around sitting.

questions.q: What does presenter James Gallagher ask Professor Edwardson?
options: Whether she sits down at work
Whether standing desks are too expensive
Whether she feels she's fighting against society
Whether new technology will solve the problem of sitting
questions.why: He asks if she feels she's swimming against the tide as society drives us to sit more.

questions.q: What simple advice does Phil give?
options: Only sit down for meals
Break up long sitting with a few minutes of moving
Exercise hard for two hours every evening after work
Stand up for the whole working day
questions.why: He says to break up sitting of 30 minutes or more with a few minutes of walking or moving.
